item.description: In a static high-angle medium shot over an L-shaped low brick wall built on sandy ground, the mason (ent_mason) bends over the outer corner. From 0.0s to 3.8s, he holds and adjusts a red brick laid on edge on the outer right face of the corner, aligning it with the adjacent header brick to form a rectangular cavity between the two parallel brick faces. From 3.8s to 5.5s, he uses his trowel (ent_trowel) to pack and smooth wet grey mortar on top of the corner joint. At 5.5s–6.5s, he reaches to the mortar pan (ent_mortar_pan) on the ground, scoops a small amount of mortar, and from 6.5s to 9.3s presses and smooths it into the vertical and top joints of the newly placed corner bricks while steadying the brick with his left hand.
item.context_result: The outer corner brick on edge is positioned and its immediate corner joint is packed with mortar, leaving two open rectangular cavities visible along the right arm of the L-shaped wall and several open cavities along the left arm.
item.camera_framing: Static high-angle medium shot looking down at the L-shaped wall corner in the foreground and the bent mason working from the upper right.
item.uncertainty: The initial placement of the brick onto the mortar bed occurred before 0.0s.

item.label: Scooping and spreading mortar bed over the corner and around cavities
item.description: Continuing in the same static framing, the mason (ent_mason) repeatedly scoops wet grey mortar from the metal pan (ent_mortar_pan) on the ground and spreads it across the top surface of the L-shaped brick-on-edge corner (ent_wall) using his trowel (ent_trowel). Between 9.3s and 11.5s he scrapes and packs mortar into the inner corner joint. He then performs seven distinct scoop-and-spread cycles from the pan to the wall: cycle 1 (11.5s–17.2s) building up the mortar bed over the corner and left-inner joint while using his left hand as a backstop; cycle 2 (17.2s–22.5s) spreading and smoothing mortar flat across the solid corner intersection; cycle 3 (22.5s–25.5s) adding mortar to the left-side brick next to the corner; cycle 4 (25.5s–28.7s) adding and smoothing more mortar across the corner top; cycle 5 (28.7s–32.7s) scooping and spreading mortar across the corner bed; cycle 6 (32.7s–41.6s, with a second quick scoop at 36.6s–38.3s) spreading mortar along the left-hand brick and then along the inner brick of the right-hand arm beside the open cavity; and cycle 7 (41.6s–46.57s) scooping mortar and spreading it along the outer brick of the right-hand arm on the other side of the cavity, with his left hand held open beside the cavity as a guard while the trowel shapes the mortar bed up to the clip end.
item.context_result: A thick grey mortar bed is progressively built up and leveled over the corner intersection and along the narrow top edges of the bricks flanking the cavities; some small mortar crumbs fall into or around the cavity edges during spreading, though the two main rectangular cavities on the right arm remain open at 46.57s when the clip cuts off mid-action.
item.camera_framing: Static high-angle medium shot; the mason's head occasionally moves above the top frame edge as heStraightens slightly between scoops.
item.uncertainty: The mortar bed preparation is still in progress when the recording ends at 46.570667s.

item.claim: The low L-shaped wall under construction demonstrates Rat-Trap Bond masonry, where bricks are laid on edge in parallel wythes connected by headers (rowlocks) to form internal hollow cavities and a staggered corner bond.
item.uncertainty: This looks like a low demonstration or practice mockup wall built directly on sandy soil rather than a full-scale building plinth, though the masonry bonding geometry itself is clearly shown.

item.claim: The mason uses his left hand alongside the brick edges and applies mortar selectively along the narrow top faces and corner headers to prepare the bed for the next course while keeping the internal cavities largely open, though small amounts of excess mortar still drop into the cavity openings.
item.uncertainty: Whether the mason later cleans out the small mortar droppings from the cavity is not seen within this clip.

claim_evidence.claim: The low brick wall arrangement illustrates the Rat-Trap Bond masonry pattern described in the script, using bricks laid on edge in parallel wythes tied by headers to create internal hollow cavities.

cues.cue: visual: In ve_01 and ent_wall, two courses of red bricks laid on edge form an L-shaped corner with alternating headers and stretchers enclosing rectangular air cavities.
script: P001 states 'Rat-Trap Bond Masonry places bricks on their edge. This arrangement creates continuous hollow cavities within the wall.'
background_knowledge: Rat-Trap Bond is a modular cavity bond in which bricks are placed on edge (shiner/rowlock orientation) creating an internal lattice of cavities.

claim_evidence.limits: Only two courses built directly on sandy soil are visible in this clip, so full-height continuous cavities across a complete building wall and structural strength are not directly established here.

claim_evidence.claim: Between 11.5s and 22.5s, the mason scoops wet mortar from the pan twice and spreads and levels a mortar bed across the 90-degree corner intersection of the brick-on-edge wall while using his left hand as a side stop.

visual: In ve_02 at 21.5s, the mason smooths the mortar bed flat across the corner intersection with the trowel.

claim_evidence.limits: At 22.5s the mason immediately reaches back to the pan for subsequent mortar cycles rather than coming to a full rest.

claim_evidence.claim: Between 32.7s and 46.570667s, the mason spreads mortar along the narrow top edges of the inner and outer bricks flanking the open rectangular cavity on the right arm of the wall, holding his left hand near the cavity edge while some small mortar crumbs still drop into the cavity.

cues.cue: visual: In ve_02 at 39.5s, the mason spreads mortar along the narrow top edge of the inner wythe brick next to the open cavity.
visual: In ve_02 at 44.5s, the mason spreads mortar along the outer wythe brick edge on the opposite side of the cavity with his left hand positioned beside the cavity opening.

claim_evidence.limits: Small fragments of mortar visibly fall into the cavity during troweling, and the clip ends at 46.570667s before the mortar bed is finished or any fallen mortar is cleared.

claim_evidence.claim: The mason's selective placement of mortar along the narrow brick edges around the open cavities illustrates the construction practice of keeping cavities open to preserve the wall's insulating properties as described in P001.
